newsitem.title: CROATIA: Privredna Banka puts company assets for sale.
newsitem.headline: Privredna Banka puts company assets for sale.

text.p: Croatia's troubled commercial bank Privredna Banka Zagreb said on Tuesday it was seeking buyers for almost one billion kuna's worth of assets in 20 firms it acquired in debt-for-equity swaps.
"This is kind of a probe, we are trying to establish what our portfolio is worth on the market," president of the board Martin Katicic told reporters.
He said the bank aimed to reduce its holdings in those companies, including department store chain NAMA and Slovenia's sports equipment manufacturer Elan.
Privredna's holdings, ranging from one to 100 percent, are being offered to both Croatian and foreign investors.
Some holdings are in indebted industries with little prospect of a speedy recovery, such as the manufacturer of heavy machinery Djuro Djakovic.
Hoping to cash in on the recovery of the tourist trade, the bank is holding back stakes it holds in hoteliers.
"But if and when a good buyer appears and offers the right price, we would also be prepared to sell our tourism portfolio," Katicic said.
